meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Внимание! = Attention!. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А ну-ка, дай посмотрю! Внимание, ребята!
examples.trans: Hold on, let me have a look! Attention, everyone!

возить.gloss: to carry, to haul, to drive (regularly)

meanings.en: to transport, to haul, to bring (repeatedly, by vehicle)
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to carry, to haul, to drive (regularly)', paired with 'везти'.

examples.text: Без него вы бы возили сувениры из Китая.
examples.trans: Without him you would be hauling souvenirs from China.
He drives the children to school.

examples.text: Мы возим её сюда специальными боингами.
examples.trans: We fly it here on special Boeings.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come in, to enter', paired with 'входить'.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact, for the record
meanings.note: Polite or pointed correction. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'лезать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'climb out'.

examples.trans: Climb out of the car quickly, terrorist.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и вылезать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and climb out on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'рубить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'shut off'.

examples.text: Вырубите дрель, я только спать лёг!
examples.trans: Turn off the drill, I just lay down to sleep!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и вырубить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and shut off on time.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm with my wife this evening.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: забирать деньги = to take the money
забирать детей из школы = to pick the kids up from school

examples.trans: I pick the children up from school.

examples.trans: And I get you a suspended sentence. Plus you take all of Vika's money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.trans: The chef always pays attention to every little detail on the plate.

examples.trans: Oh, that happens very often, Arkashenka. Bellowing songs!

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

потерпеть.gloss: to be patient for a while, to endure

meanings.en: to be patient for a little while, to hold on
meanings.note: Often imperative: потерпи!. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терпеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be patient for a while, to endure', paired with 'терпеть'.

examples.text: Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: We need to be patient a little and work a bit.

examples.text: Послушай меня, Ваня. Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: Listen to me, Vanya. We need to be patient a little and work a bit.

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: имей совесть! = have a heart! / shame on you!

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'уббота'). Common feminine noun meaning 'Saturday' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Скажи всем ребятам, что в субботу вечером будет вечеринка.

examples.text: Каждую субботу в нашем ресторане бронируют абсолютно все столики.
examples.trans: Every Saturday absolutely all the tables in our restaurant are booked.

meanings.en: twenty-four-hour period, full day and night
meanings.note: plural-only noun; used with collective numerals like двое суток

examples.text: Так точно, товарищ генерал! Мы вторые сутки не спим.

meanings.note: Cab vehicle for hire. Common neuter noun meaning 'taxi; cab' in everyday Russian.
